hints: Focus on what 3.00% by mass really means for 1 tonne of ore, and remember only part of that copper carbonate is copper.
Start by finding the mass of pure CuCO3 in 1 tonne (1000 kg), then work out its molar mass using Cu = 63.5, C = 12.0, O = 16.0.
Use moles to link the mass of CuCO3 to the mass of Cu inside it, since 1 mol of CuCO3 contains 1 mol of Cu atoms.
walkthrough:
**Find the mass of pure copper carbonate in the ore**

You have 1 tonne of ore, which is 1000 kg. Only 3.00% of this is useful $\text{CuCO}_3$.

$$\text{mass of CuCO}_3 = \frac{3.00}{100} \times 1000 \text{ kg} = 30.0 \text{ kg} = 30000 \text{ g}$$

**Calculate the molar masses**

One formula unit of copper carbonate contains one copper atom, so we compare their masses.

$$M_r(\text{CuCO}_3) = 63.5 + 12.0 + (3 \times 16.0) = 123.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$$

$$A_r(\text{Cu}) = 63.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$$

**Convert carbonate to copper using moles**

First find moles of carbonate, then convert to mass of copper. The mole ratio is 1:1.

$$\text{moles CuCO}_3 = \frac{30000}{123.5} = 242.9 \text{ mol}$$

$$\text{mass Cu} = 242.9 \times 63.5 = 15424 \text{ g} \approx 15.4 \text{ kg}$$

**Choose the matching answer**

About 15.4 kg of copper can be obtained. This makes sense because just over half of the 30 kg of carbonate is copper.

options.A: Too small by almost a factor of 10. Often comes from a unit slip with tonnes and kilograms, for example treating 1 tonne as 100 kg or misplacing a decimal when converting 30.0 kg to grams.
options.B: Much too small. This type of value comes from using the wrong part of the compound, for example calculating the mass of carbon or oxygen instead of copper, or dividing by the molar mass instead of multiplying correctly.
options.C: Correct. 30.0 kg of CuCO3 contains 242.9 mol, which gives 242.9 mol of Cu. That is about 15.4 kg, just over half of 30 kg because copper (63.5) is just over half of the Mr (123.5).
options.D: Too large, almost double the total mass of CuCO3 present (30 kg). This comes from inverting the mass fraction, using 123.5/63.5 instead of 63.5/123.5, which incorrectly makes the copper heavier than the compound it comes from.
